document:653.text:
Dear stranger,
By the time you find this, I'll probably be gone.
When I learned how ill I was, I couldn't take it in. Death was something that happened to other people. Surely it couldn't be happening to me.
I'd always been lucky. Every bet I made went my way, and I never lost a coin at the card table. Then I sat down across from the God of Death with my life at stake, and there wasn't a thing I could do to win.
But here's a thought, my friend. What if life was only ever a loan from the God of Death? Perhaps mine has simply come due. I find that a little easier to accept.
I wonder who you are. Whoever finds this, I suppose a reply is out of the question.
When you've finished reading, my friend, please put this letter back in its bottle and send it out to sea. Let it drift wherever the current takes it. Isn't that what we've all been doing, in our own way?
document:653.source_cn:
亲爱的陌生人：
当你捡到它的时候，我大概已经不在人世了。
得知我已身患重病的消息时，我犹如五雷轰顶，不肯相信死亡这种事怎么会降临到我身上。
我一向是个幸运的人，跟别人打赌永远会赢，打牌也从未输过钱，可在跟死神用生命做赌注的这一场赌局里，我竟然就这样无能为力地输了。
嘿，朋友，你有没有想过，我们的生命本就是向死神借来的？这样想来，我似乎也能够更加坦率地去面对死亡了。
不知道这封信会被谁捡到，捡到了也没办法给我回信，对吧？
亲爱的朋友，等你读完这封信时，请将它装回瓶子里去，让它继续在海上漫无目的地飘荡吧。就好像我们这一生，都在生命的长河里漫无目的地飘荡。
